Rabivy AI Engine - Maintenance Dashboard

What the dashboard shows, tab by tab, and what it takes to keep it accurate

Author

Tilabo Williamson, Caitlin Buenk & Jürgen Becker (Project Lead) - AX Consult Group

Published

2026-08-05

Project Overview Evaluation Suite Live Queries and RLHF Maintenance Dashboard

AX Consult Group - commercial showcase.

The Evaluation Suite page covers the golden 30 under controlled conditions, and the Live Queries and RLHF page covers how a real question gets classified and reviewed. The dashboard is where all of that actually lives day to day - one page, three tabs, built from real logs rather than a mockup.

The three tabs

  • Golden Test Set - the same fixed 30 questions from the Evaluation Suite page, run under controlled conditions. This is the only tab where every result is already known and verified ahead of time.
  • Live Queries - every real question that’s ever come in, classified only by the four automatic gates from the Live Queries and RLHF page. No human judgement involved, which also means it can’t reliably say whether an answer’s content was actually right - only whether the process behind it looked healthy. A KPI box on this tab shows what fraction of all live questions have actually been reviewed through RLHF.
  • RLHF feedback - only the subset of live questions a rep has actually reviewed, classified using the eight outcomes described on the Live Queries and RLHF page instead of plain gate status. This is the only tab where “correct” or “wrong” reflects an actual person’s judgement rather than an automated check.

Live Queries and RLHF feedback are kept as two separate tabs on purpose, rather than merged into one - conflating “passed the automatic checks” with “a human confirmed this was right” would overstate what the gates alone can actually tell you. Where the two do connect: a reviewed row on the Live Queries tab links straight through to its full entry on the RLHF tab, so nothing needs to be found twice.

The golden test set’s decision tree

The Golden Test Set tab has its own decision tree, walking through the same three-layer check the Evaluation Suite page describes for every golden-30 run - Routing, Rules, Answer - down to a final pass/fail outcome for each question. However, within those 3 layers are different types of passes and fails. For example, hallucination is an example of layer 1 and or 2 failing (no evidence surfaced) but the engine giving an incorrect answer anyway.

See the figure below for the golden test set decision tree.

Green - System worked. No action needed.

Amber - System partially working. Live flag. Potential review/batch review. Track prevalence over time.

Red - System not working. Live flag. Block Answer. Review all occurrences. Track prevalence over time.

The Golden Test Set Tab

Below is a screenshot of the KPI boxes highlighting key metrics within the golden test set.

Keeping it current

The dashboard is a static file (dashboard.html), rebuilt by running python build_dashboard.py - it isn’t wired into any automatic pipeline yet, so it only reflects data as of whenever it was last rebuilt and pushed. A few things worth knowing about what that actually involves:

  • The two logs are the real source of truth. output/QUERY_LOG/query_log.jsonl (every question) and output/RLHF_FEEDBACK/rlhf_log.jsonl (only the reviewed ones) hold the raw data. build_dashboard.py reads both fresh every time it runs and rebuilds dashboard.html from scratch - nothing on the page updates on its own between rebuilds.
  • Labels are recomputed fresh, not trusted from storage. Every time the dashboard is rebuilt, each reviewed question’s classification is recalculated from its raw stored fields (rating, evidence answer, whether the engine actually declined), rather than reusing whatever label was saved at the moment a rep submitted their review. That means a genuine logic fix - like the decline-flow fix or the retrieval-confidence gate fix described on the RLHF page - automatically corrects how existing entries get read the next time the dashboard is rebuilt.
  • That only goes so far. If a rep’s underlying answer was itself captured wrong under an old, confusing version of the review flow - not just read wrong by old logic - rebuilding the dashboard can’t fix that on its own. That entry needs a rep to actually look at the question again and re-submit a review through the current flow.
  • Rebuilding and pushing is a manual step today. After any change to the gate logic, the RLHF scoring, or a batch of new reviews worth surfacing, someone needs to run the build and commit the refreshed dashboard.html - there’s no CI job or scheduled rebuild doing this automatically yet.

AX Consult Group. Rabivy is used here as a commercial analytics showcase and is not intended for clinical use.

## Keeping it current

The dashboard is a static file (`dashboard.html`), rebuilt by running
`python build_dashboard.py` - it isn't wired into any automatic pipeline
yet, so it only reflects data as of whenever it was last rebuilt and
pushed. A few things worth knowing about what that actually involves:

- **The two logs are the real source of truth.**
  `output/QUERY_LOG/query_log.jsonl` (every question) and
  `output/RLHF_FEEDBACK/rlhf_log.jsonl` (only the reviewed ones) hold
  the raw data. `build_dashboard.py` reads both fresh every time it runs
  and rebuilds `dashboard.html` from scratch - nothing on the page
  updates on its own between rebuilds.
- **Labels are recomputed fresh, not trusted from storage.** Every time
  the dashboard is rebuilt, each reviewed question's classification is
  recalculated from its raw stored fields (rating, evidence answer,
  whether the engine actually declined), rather than reusing whatever
  label was saved at the moment a rep submitted their review. That means
  a genuine logic fix - like the decline-flow fix or the
  retrieval-confidence gate fix described on the
  [RLHF](live_queries_&_RLHF.html) page - automatically corrects how
  *existing* entries get read the next
  time the dashboard is rebuilt.
- **That only goes so far.** If a rep's underlying answer was itself
  captured wrong under an old, confusing version of the review flow -
  not just read wrong by old logic - rebuilding the dashboard can't fix
  that on its own. That entry needs a rep to actually look at the
  question again and re-submit a review through the current flow.
- **Rebuilding and pushing is a manual step today.** After any change to
  the gate logic, the RLHF scoring, or a batch of new reviews worth
  surfacing, someone needs to run the build and commit the refreshed
  `dashboard.html` - there's no CI job or scheduled rebuild doing this
  automatically yet.
